Around the Earth, a ribbon was stretched along the equator. Then the length of the ribbon was increased by 1 meter and it was again evenly placed around the equator. Will a cat be able to pass through the resulting gap?

Yes, a cat would be able to pass through the gap. When we add 1 meter to the ribbon around the Earth's equator, it creates a gap of approximately 16 centimeters (about 1/(2π) meters) all around. This is calculated by noting that if the original circumference is 2πR and the new circumference is 2πR + 1, the difference in radius is 1/(2π) ≈ 0.159 meters or about 16 cm. Since most cats can fit through openings of 10-15 cm, a cat would be able to pass through this gap.
